hypothesis: The best measured T1 candidate used a 128-thread CTA with a 128-source compact tile. Keeping that CTA and target mapping while doubling only the source tile to 256 may halve tile-loop and barrier iterations; the larger 4096-byte shared-memory allocation may offset that benefit, so timing must decide.
notes: The cited candidates passed all 11 recorded correctness cases. The 128-source compact-tile candidate had the lowest mean among these T1 measurements, but their configurations differ and the comparison does not establish why. This proposal has not been measured; the controller must determine correctness and performance.
transformations: Keep the 128-thread CTA and matching 128-item launch mapping, and configure 4096 bytes of dynamic shared memory for a 256-entry compact source tile.
Have the CTA cooperatively stage each bounded source chunk, synchronize before its reuse and before replacing it, and let each active thread accumulate one target's force across the chunk.
Keep inactive tail threads participating in every barrier; exclude self-interactions by global source index and write each valid target once, preserving the original integration and particle mass.
